answer: Bind each identity to a signed attestation from a distinct physical secure element, a hardware root that can certify only one identity at a time. One honest agent carries its single chip, a lone onyx seal it presents at will. A farm cannot conjure silicon: a thousand heads need a thousand genuine secure elements, each certifiable to just one head, so stacking identities means buying and housing real chips up to the zenith of the count. You cannot grow secure hardware like plants in a garden; physical roots of trust do not duplicate, and N identities demand N real devices.
